goal: Load and continuously refresh ColdLion /prepackDetail data in the live coldlion.prepack_detail table created by #2863: extend the existing repository-owned ColdLion landing loader (no second framework), add synthetic offline tests, and wire a bounded, resumable production backfill plus the ongoing scheduled refresh. No database-shape change.
dispatcher: delegated source-data session started from issue #3179 text (non-orchestrator work)
prohibited_actions: Never author a migration or change any database shape; this work changes rows and loader code only (issue #3179 db-work-scope declares writes: []).
Never run the loader against a database whose connection string does not name the declared COLDLION_EXPECTED_PROJECT_REF; the target is proved immediately before every write.
Never commit ColdLion row values, harvested key populations, or credentials; fixtures are synthetic and logs carry counts only.
Never close issue #3179; the originating session owns closure.
assumptions: The /prepackDetail shape and grain are those sampled live on 2026-09-15 (docs/coldlion-unit-5b-grain-proof-20260915.md): a bare JSON array of eighteen fields keyed by (company_code, prepack_code, sequence_no), with itemPrice and ItemPrice as two real properties.

The complete approved prepackCode population is harvestable from already-landed ColdLion data (issue #3179 required work); coldlion.inventory and coldlion.prod_detail contribute automatically once their own loaders exist.
Resumability needs no schema change: every successful run records the cumulative covered key set in coldlion.sync_run.request_params.
A zero-row response for a harvested code is expected and must be counted and named, never silently skipped; malformed responses abort the run before any write.
stop_conditions: Stop and report a blocker if the live dry-run shows a response shape outside the eighteen-field sample or a harvest population too large for the scheduled window.
Stop on any unresolved guard or reviewer refusal; a new head answering it requires a fresh exact-head review.
